responsibility: This module is GCC’s language-independent diagnostics subsystem: it owns the central diagnostics::context and diagnostic_info pipeline for classifying, counting, buffering, and emitting warnings, errors, notes, paths, and related metadata, while providing the shared policies that control columns, source quoting, colors, URLs, option-based severity overrides, and source-file access. Its main file families divide into core context/state management (context, kinds, counters, option-classifier, option-id), source-location and fix-it presentation (file-cache, source-printing, column/context/source-printing option headers, macro-unwinding, changes), abstract output and sink selection (sink, output-spec, output-file), concrete output backends for classic text, SARIF, and HTML (text-sink, sarif-sink, html-sink, color), and richer structured attachments such as paths, lazy paths, logical locations, metadata, digraphs, diagrams, and analyzer-oriented state graphs with dot export. Supporting dumping and selftest files provide debugging and verification infrastructure, but the stable responsibility of the module is to turn internal compiler diagnostic events into consistently formatted human-readable and machine-readable reports, including caret/source snippets, fix-it edits, path explanations, and structured metadata, independently of any specific GCC front end or target.
